edition_identification.answer: The current game is Pathfinder Second Edition using the Remastered rules. The remaster is a revision of Second Edition, not a separate Pathfinder Third Edition.

core_remastered_books.purpose: Primary player rules, character creation, eight core classes, feats, spells, equipment, and playing procedures.
Game Master procedures, encounter and adventure tools, subsystems, hazards, treasure guidance, and campaign operation.
Eight additional remastered classes plus more player options.

compatibility_summary: Most pre-remaster Pathfinder Second Edition material remains mechanically usable.
Use remastered terminology and current errata when an old term or rule has been replaced.
Some options need a compatibility interpretation because alignment, spell schools, damage terminology, and certain names changed.
A Game Master should announce whether legacy options are allowed and how conflicts with remastered text will be resolved.

play_loop: The Game Master describes the situation.
Players say what their characters attempt.
If success is uncertain and meaningful, roll a check.
Roll d20, add the relevant modifier, and compare the total with a Difficulty Class.
Determine critical success, success, failure, or critical failure.
Apply the result, update the fiction, and continue.
thirty_second_summary.encounter_turn: At the start of a normal turn, you receive 3 actions and can normally use 1 reaction before your next turn if a trigger allows it.
thirty_second_summary.key_tactical_lesson: Pathfinder rewards teamwork and varied actions. Moving, making a target off-guard, Demoralizing, Raising a Shield, Aiding, or Recall Knowledge can be better than making a heavily penalized third attack.
thirty_second_summary.key_character_lesson: Your ancestry, background, and class define your foundation; feats let you customize rather than forcing every member of a class into the same build.

core_resolution_system.standard_check_formula: d20 + relevant modifier versus a Difficulty Class

degrees_of_success.critical_success: Your total is at least 10 higher than the DC.
degrees_of_success.success: Your total equals or exceeds the DC, but is not a critical success.
degrees_of_success.failure: Your total is below the DC, but not a critical failure.
degrees_of_success.critical_failure: Your total is at least 10 lower than the DC.

natural_die_adjustments.natural_20: Improve the degree of success by one step after comparing the total to the DC.
natural_die_adjustments.natural_1: Worsen the degree of success by one step after comparing the total to the DC.
natural_die_adjustments.important_note: A natural 20 is not always automatically a critical success, and a natural 1 is not always automatically a critical failure; they shift the calculated degree by one step.

common_check_types.saving_throw: A Fortitude, Reflex, or Will check against an effect's DC.
common_check_types.skill_check: A check using a skill modifier against a DC.
common_check_types.perception_check: A check to notice, search, detect, or act in initiative.
common_check_types.counteract_check: A specialized check used to remove or suppress certain magical or harmful effects.
common_check_types.flat_check: A d20 roll without modifiers; success occurs by meeting the listed flat DC.

basic_saving_throw.note: Only use this four-result damage pattern when an effect calls for a basic save.

core_resolution_system.dc_from_modifier: When a rule converts a modifier into a DC, the DC is usually 10 plus that modifier.
core_resolution_system.specific_over_general: When a specific ability conflicts with a general rule, the specific ability normally controls.
core_resolution_system.secret_checks: For actions whose uncertainty would be spoiled by seeing the die, the GM may roll secretly. The character still acts on what they perceive, not on the player's knowledge of the number.

fortune_and_misfortune.fortune: Changes how a roll is made in a beneficial way, often by allowing another roll or choosing a result.
fortune_and_misfortune.misfortune: Changes how a roll is made in a harmful way.
fortune_and_misfortune.interaction: Multiple fortune effects do not normally stack on one roll, multiple misfortune effects do not normally stack, and a fortune and misfortune effect can cancel.

attribute_modifiers.Strength: Physical power; common for melee attacks, damage, Athletics, and carrying capacity.
attribute_modifiers.Dexterity: Agility and precision; common for AC, Reflex, ranged attacks, Acrobatics, Stealth, and Thievery.
attribute_modifiers.Constitution: Endurance; contributes to HP and Fortitude.
attribute_modifiers.Intelligence: Reasoning and learned knowledge; common for Arcana, Crafting, Occultism, Society, and Lore.
attribute_modifiers.Wisdom: Awareness and intuition; common for Perception, Will, Medicine, Nature, Religion, and Survival.
attribute_modifiers.Charisma: Presence and force of personality; common for Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, and Performance.

untrained.meaning: No level is added unless a specific rule says otherwise.

typed_modifiers.stacking_rule: For bonuses of the same type, use only the highest. For penalties of the same type, use only the worst. Bonuses and penalties of different types can combine.
typed_modifiers.untyped_rule: Untyped modifiers generally combine unless their specific rules say otherwise.

common_formulas.armor_class: 10 + Dexterity modifier up to armor's cap + proficiency bonus + armor item bonus + other modifiers
common_formulas.fortitude: Constitution modifier + proficiency bonus + other modifiers
common_formulas.reflex: Dexterity modifier + proficiency bonus + other modifiers
common_formulas.will: Wisdom modifier + proficiency bonus + other modifiers
common_formulas.perception: Wisdom modifier + proficiency bonus + other modifiers
common_formulas.skill: key attribute modifier + proficiency bonus + other modifiers
common_formulas.melee_attack: d20 + Strength modifier + proficiency bonus + other modifiers; finesse can allow Dexterity for the attack roll
common_formulas.ranged_attack: d20 + Dexterity modifier + proficiency bonus + other modifiers
common_formulas.spell_attack: d20 + spellcasting attribute modifier + spellcasting proficiency + other modifiers
common_formulas.spell_dc: 10 + spellcasting attribute modifier + spellcasting proficiency + other modifiers
common_formulas.class_dc: 10 + class key attribute modifier + class DC proficiency + other modifiers

character_creation.overview: Create a coherent concept, then make rules choices in the order below. Record each choice immediately because later numbers depend on earlier choices.

steps.name: Create a concept
instructions: Choose a broad fantasy, personality, and party role.
Ask what the campaign is about and why this character will cooperate with the group.
Select a tentative class before optimizing attributes.
steps.example: A former border scout who protects travelers and studies dangerous beasts.

steps.name: Choose an ancestry
instructions: Record ancestry Hit Points, size, Speed, languages, traits, and special abilities.
Apply ancestry attribute boosts and flaws, or use the permitted alternative of two free boosts.
Select a heritage.
Select a 1st-level ancestry feat.
steps.design_question: What physical, cultural, or supernatural inheritance shapes the character?

steps.name: Choose a background
instructions: Apply its two attribute boosts as instructed.
Record the trained skill.
Record the trained Lore skill.
Record the granted skill feat.
steps.design_question: What did the character do before adventuring?

steps.name: Choose a class
instructions: Apply the class's key attribute boost.
Record class Hit Points per level.
Record initial proficiencies.
Record class features, subclass-like choice, spells, formulas, companion, or other required choices.
Choose the class feat or other 1st-level options the class grants.
steps.design_question: What does the character reliably contribute when danger begins?

steps.name: Apply four free attribute boosts
instructions: Choose four different attributes.
Do not apply more than one of these four boosts to the same attribute.
At 1st level, a normal character's highest attribute modifier is generally +4.
priority_advice: Ensure enough Dexterity for the intended armor and Reflex defense.
Value Constitution for HP and Fortitude.
Support the skills and role the character will use often.

steps.name: Calculate details
instructions: Calculate maximum HP.
Calculate Perception and saving throws.
Calculate AC.
Calculate weapon attacks and damage.
Calculate skill modifiers.
Record class DC and spell attack/DC when applicable.

steps.name: Buy equipment
instructions: A normal 1st-level character begins with 15 gp unless the campaign says otherwise.
Buy an appropriate weapon or spellcasting equipment.
Buy armor if the build uses it.
Buy an adventurer's pack or equivalent essentials.
Reserve money for class tools, ammunition, healer's tools, thieves' tools, shield, or formula-related needs.
avoid: Do not buy armor you are not proficient with without understanding the cost.
Do not exceed Bulk capacity without planning for encumbered.
Do not assume every shield can use Shield Block; the character needs the feat or another permission.

steps.name: Finish identity and campaign links
instructions: Choose name, age, pronouns, appearance, beliefs, and personality.
Record languages.
Create at least one relationship to another character or campaign element.
Explain why the character accepts the opening adventure.

hit_point_formula.level_1: ancestry HP + class HP + Constitution contribution specified by the class rules
hit_point_formula.later_levels: gain the class's HP per level plus the Constitution contribution specified by the class rules
hit_point_formula.note: Use the exact class and character-creation text when calculating; character builders can verify the arithmetic.

starting_resources.wealth: 15 gp at 1st level under the standard creation rules
starting_resources.hero_points: A character normally begins a game session with 1 Hero Point and can hold up to 3.
starting_resources.spellcasters: Prepare spells or confirm the spell repertoire and daily slots.
starting_resources.invested_items: Daily preparations allow investment in up to 10 worn items unless a rule changes the limit.

build_validation_checklist: The class key attribute is as high as the concept reasonably allows.
Every boost has been applied once and only where legal.
Ancestry, heritage, ancestry feat, background, class choices, and class feat are recorded.
All trained skills and Lore skills are marked.
Armor proficiency and Dexterity cap are reflected in AC.
Weapon proficiency and weapon traits are recorded.
At least one useful encounter action does not require attacking.
The character has a useful exploration activity.
The party has a plan for healing between encounters.
The character has a reason to cooperate with the group.

classes.classification_note: The class list reflects the current Archives of Nethys class index as checked on the verification date. Complexity ratings are editorial learning estimates, not official Paizo labels.

beginner_friendly_editorial_recommendati.why: Accurate weapon attacks, durable fundamentals, and tactical depth without spell preparation.
Clear Hunt Prey loop, good weapons, useful exploration identity, and multiple build directions.
Many skills and a teamwork-focused combat goal: attack off-guard enemies.
Direct melee role with a clear Rage mode and satisfying damage.
A comparatively approachable spellcaster whose composition magic gives a reliable default action.
A clear divine support identity, strong healing options, and prepared flexibility.

entries.name: Alchemist
entries.beginner_note: Best for a player who enjoys planning, item catalogs, and adapting daily resources.

entries.name: Animist
entries.beginner_note: Requires learning prepared magic plus a flexible apparition subsystem.

entries.name: Barbarian
entries.beginner_note: A direct martial choice; learn when to Rage and how to manage its restrictions.

entries.name: Bard
entries.beginner_note: A strong first caster for players who like supporting the entire party each round.

entries.name: Champion
entries.beginner_note: Good for learning positioning because the class rewards protecting nearby allies.

entries.name: Cleric
entries.beginner_note: A capable first prepared caster when the player wants a clear support role.

entries.name: Commander
entries.beginner_note: Works best for a player who knows the party's capabilities and enjoys team-wide planning.

entries.name: Druid
entries.beginner_note: Broad spell access makes the class flexible but increases preparation choices.

entries.name: Exemplar
entries.beginner_note: The turn-to-turn ikon state rewards system familiarity.

entries.name: Fighter
typical_party_contributions: battlefield control through feats and reactions
entries.beginner_note: One of the easiest entry points while still offering deep tactical growth.

entries.name: Guardian
entries.beginner_note: Good for a defensive player who pays attention to positioning and enemy threats.

entries.name: Gunslinger
entries.beginner_note: Requires careful action planning because firing and reloading compete for actions.

entries.name: Inventor
entries.beginner_note: Best for players who enjoy customization and managing risk-reward abilities.

entries.name: Investigator
entries.beginner_note: Rewards using information and choosing an alternate plan when a predicted attack is poor.

entries.name: Kineticist
typical_party_contributions: defense or healing depending on elements
entries.beginner_note: Does not use normal spell slots, but has many trait and impulse interactions to learn.

entries.name: Magus
entries.beginner_note: Powerful but action-tight; the player must plan Spellstrike, recharge, movement, and defense.

entries.name: Monk
entries.beginner_note: Flurry of Blows leaves actions free for movement, defense, or maneuvers.

entries.name: Oracle
entries.beginner_note: A player must understand both spontaneous spellcasting and the class's curse interactions.

entries.name: Psychic
entries.beginner_note: Timing Unleash Psyche and focus resources adds a distinct rhythm.

entries.name: Ranger
entries.beginner_note: A good first class; remember to Hunt Prey before using many class benefits.

entries.name: Rogue
entries.beginner_note: Teaches teamwork because off-guard enemies enable the rogue's signature damage.

entries.name: Sorcerer
entries.beginner_note: Less daily preparation than a wizard, but spell-repertoire choices matter for many levels.

entries.name: Summoner
entries.beginner_note: The shared action pool and two bodies create one of the game's most unusual turn structures.

entries.name: Swashbuckler
entries.beginner_note: The player alternates between gaining panache and spending it on finishers.

entries.name: Thaumaturge
entries.beginner_note: Implement choices and special weakness rules reward a careful reader.

entries.name: Witch
entries.beginner_note: Prepared spells, familiar rules, patron lessons, and hex timing create several moving parts.

entries.name: Wizard
entries.beginner_note: Very flexible, but the player must learn a large spell list and prepare effectively.

recall_knowledge.purpose: Identify creatures, magic, hazards, organizations, history, or other useful facts.

Lore: the narrow subject named by the Lore skill

table_practice: Tell the GM what you are trying to learn.
The GM selects the skill and DC, often rolling secretly.
A more specific Lore can receive an easier DC than a broad skill.
Useful facts should inform tactics, negotiation, or exploration rather than merely naming a creature.

medicine_and_recovery.importance: A party that can Treat Wounds is much more resilient between encounters.
recommended_party_plan: Have at least one trained Medicine user with healer's tools, a magical healer, or another reliable recovery method.
Track immunity periods created by Treat Wounds.
Allow time after hard encounters unless the situation is intentionally urgent.
medicine_and_recovery.rules_note: Use the current Medicine skill entry for exact DCs, healing dice, immunity, and feat upgrades.

aid.purpose: Prepare to help another creature with a check.
procedure_summary: Prepare using the Aid action or the procedure specified by the GM.
Use a reaction when the ally makes the aided check.
The GM chooses a relevant skill or attack roll and DC.
Success usually grants a circumstance bonus; critical success grants a larger bonus based on proficiency.

used_for: chases or tense sequences needing precise turns
encounter.structure: Initiative order, one turn per participant each round, 3 actions on a normal turn, and reactions when triggered.

exploration.structure: Each character usually focuses on one exploration activity while the GM advances time and describes discoveries.

downtime.structure: Resolve long-term activities in larger time increments.

transition_examples: While Avoiding Notice in exploration, a character may roll Stealth for initiative when an encounter begins.
A character using Defend can begin an encounter with a shield already raised, subject to the activity.
After an encounter, the group may return to exploration, Treat Wounds, Refocus, Search, and decide whether to continue.

initiative.alternate_checks: The GM can allow another skill that matches the approach, such as Stealth when Avoiding Notice or Deception during a social distraction.
initiative.order: Highest result acts first, then descending.
initiative.surprise_note: Pathfinder normally represents readiness through initiative skills, detection states, and encounter positioning rather than a universal surprise round.

start_of_turn: Resolve effects that occur at the start of your turn.
Regain actions, usually 3, reduced or increased by conditions such as slowed, stunned, or quickened.
Regain the ability to use a reaction if nothing says otherwise.
during_turn: Spend actions in any legal order.
One-action, two-action, and three-action activities cost the indicated number of actions.
Free actions cost no action but still require their trigger or timing.
You do not have to spend every action.
end_of_turn: Attempt flat checks to end persistent damage.
Reduce frightened if its normal rule applies.

universal_action_types.activity: Costs the displayed number of actions and must be completed as one unit.
universal_action_types.reaction: Used when its trigger occurs; normally one is available between the starts of your turns.
universal_action_types.free_action: Costs no action but can have a trigger, frequency, or timing restriction.

notes: Movement can trigger reactions if their triggers apply.
Difficult terrain increases movement cost.

Step.effect: Move 5 feet without triggering reactions caused by movement.
notes: You normally cannot Step into difficult terrain.
Some abilities increase Step distance.

Strike.effect: Make a weapon or unarmed attack against AC.

degrees.critical_failure: Usually no additional effect unless a rule says otherwise.

Interact.effect: Manipulate an object, such as drawing an item, opening an uncomplicated door, or retrieving something accessible.
notes: Has the manipulate trait and can trigger relevant reactions.
Dropping an item is normally a free action rather than Interact.

Raise_a_Shield.effect: Gain the shield's circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.
notes: Shield Block is a separate reaction and requires access to that feat or ability.
A raised shield is not automatically blocking damage.

Take_Cover.effect: Improve the defensive benefit of available cover, or gain cover in a position that permits it.
notes: Standard cover commonly gives +2 circumstance AC, Reflex against area effects, and Stealth.
The exact result depends on existing cover and position.

Escape.effect: Attempt to end grabbed, immobilized, or restrained using an allowed unarmed attack modifier, Acrobatics, or Athletics.
notes: Has the attack trait and therefore contributes to multiple attack penalty.

Delay.cost: free action at the start of your turn
Delay.effect: Leave initiative and re-enter later, permanently changing your initiative position for the encounter.
notes: You cannot Delay after using actions on the turn.
Some start- or end-of-turn effects still require careful adjudication.

Ready.effect: Choose a single action and a trigger; when the trigger occurs before your next turn, use a reaction to perform the chosen action.
notes: The readied action must normally be a single action.
Ready is useful for timing, but expensive in actions and reaction use.

Aid.cost: usually 1 action to prepare and a reaction to help
Aid.effect: Attempt to grant an ally a circumstance bonus to a check.
notes: Describe a plausible method.
The GM determines the check and DC.

Seek.effect: Scan an area using Perception to find hidden, undetected, or unnoticed creatures or objects.
notes: The search area depends on the sense and direction.
The GM often rolls secret checks for hidden information.

Recall_Knowledge.effect: Use an appropriate knowledge skill to remember useful information.
notes: Often secret.
Ask a tactical or investigative question rather than only requesting a name.

multiple_attack_penalty.when_it_applies: Each action with the attack trait after the first attack on your turn takes a penalty.
important_examples: Strike, Grapple, Shove, Trip, Escape, and spell attack rolls can all have the attack trait.
A missed first attack still counts.
Most attacks made outside your turn do not use or increase your multiple attack penalty unless a rule says otherwise.
multiple_attack_penalty.beginner_advice: A third attack is often less valuable than movement, defense, Recall Knowledge, Demoralize, Aid, Feint, or another setup action.

movement_and_space.difficult_terrain: Each square or distance costs extra movement as defined by the terrain.
movement_and_space.forced_movement: Usually does not trigger reactions based on voluntarily moving unless the reaction says otherwise.
movement_and_space.diagonal_movement: Use the table's chosen grid procedure and the current movement rules.
movement_and_space.reach: A creature threatens or targets spaces within its listed reach; size alone does not guarantee greater reach.

flanking.summary: Two allies on opposite sides of a creature can make it off-guard to their melee attacks when all flanking requirements are met.
flanking.effect: Off-guard imposes a -2 circumstance penalty to AC.
flanking.teamwork_value: Flanking improves accuracy and critical chance and can activate precision effects.

cover.standard_cover: +2 circumstance bonus to AC, Reflex saves against area effects, and Stealth checks to Hide
cover.note: Line geometry, creature size, obstacles, and Take Cover determine the actual benefit.

positioning.line_of_effect: Most attacks and spells need an unobstructed path for the effect, even when the target is visible.
positioning.line_of_sight: Visual targeting usually requires the target to be perceived, though senses and specific abilities can change this.

common_combat_skill_actions.Demoralize: Use Intimidation to make a creature frightened; it is especially useful before allies attack.
common_combat_skill_actions.Feint: Use Deception to make a target off-guard to your next melee attack under the action's rules.
common_combat_skill_actions.Grapple: Use Athletics against Fortitude DC to grab or restrain.
common_combat_skill_actions.Reposition: Use Athletics to move a grabbed or accessible target according to the action.
common_combat_skill_actions.Shove: Use Athletics against Fortitude DC to push a target.
common_combat_skill_actions.Trip: Use Athletics against Reflex DC to knock a target prone.
common_combat_skill_actions.Tumble_Through: Use Acrobatics to move through an enemy's space.

sample_rounds.why_it_works: One accurate attack plus positioning and defense is reliable and protects the next round.

actions: Tumble Through to reach the opposite side
Step away or use a skill action
sample_rounds.why_it_works: The rogue creates or exploits off-guard and avoids wasting a low-accuracy third attack.
The composition supports allies while the spell provides offense, control, or utility.
The setup activates class features; later turns can spend more actions attacking or repositioning.

actions: use a legal healing action or activity
Raise a Shield, Step, or prepare support
sample_rounds.why_it_works: Recovery preserves the party's action economy and prevents dying.

damage_sequence: Apply weaknesses, resistances, and immunities in the order specified by the damage rules.
Reduce current Hit Points by remaining damage.
If a player character reaches 0 HP, apply knockout and dying rules.
damage_healing_and_death.critical_damage: A critical Strike normally deals double damage. Apply the rule's specified doubling method and any exceptions.
temporary_hit_points: They are lost before normal HP.
Temporary HP from multiple sources normally do not add together; keep the higher pool unless a rule says otherwise.
They cannot exceed their own duration.

initial_dying: When reduced to 0 HP, move your initiative position to immediately before the creature or effect that reduced you to 0, if applicable.
You instead usually gain dying 2 if the knockout came from an attacker's critical success or your critical failure.
Add your wounded value to the dying value gained.

recovery_check.timing: At the start of your turn while dying.
recovery_check.check: Flat check with DC 10 + current dying value.

zero_hp_and_dying.damage_while_dying: Taking damage while dying normally increases dying by 1, or by 2 for damage from an attacker's critical success or your own critical failure.
zero_hp_and_dying.death_threshold: Dying 4 normally means death. Doomed lowers the threshold.
zero_hp_and_dying.losing_dying: When dying is removed, you normally gain wounded 1 or increase wounded by 1.

hero_points.reroll: Spend 1 Hero Point to reroll a check and use the new result, following the fortune-effect rules.
hero_points.heroic_recovery: Spend all Hero Points, with at least 1 available, to avoid death: lose dying and do not gain wounded from that recovery.
hero_points.gm_awards: The GM can award additional Hero Points during play for significant accomplishments, heroic actions, or supporting the game.

wounded_and_doomed.wounded: Makes the next knockout start at a higher dying value.
wounded_and_doomed.clearing_wounded: Commonly ends after successful Treat Wounds that restores HP, or after reaching full HP and resting for 10 minutes.
wounded_and_doomed.doomed: Lowers the dying value at which the character dies.

damage_healing_and_death.massive_damage: A creature can die instantly when one damage instance equals or exceeds twice its maximum HP, subject to the full rule and exceptions.
party_recovery_plan: Carry healer's tools if using Medicine.
Identify which characters can heal during combat and which heal only between encounters.
After a knockout, clear wounded before another dangerous fight when time permits.
Refocus and repair shields while Medicine users Treat Wounds.
Do not assume every encounter is balanced around entering at low HP.

core_procedure: The GM describes the route, environment, and pace.
Each character states an exploration activity or another specific task.
The GM advances time, makes secret checks when needed, and reveals events.
When precise timing matters, transition to encounter mode.

Avoid_Notice.effect_summary: Move at a reduced exploration pace and use Stealth to remain unnoticed. You can often roll Stealth for initiative.
Avoid_Notice.best_user: A scout or character expecting ambushes.

Defend.effect_summary: Move at reduced pace and begin a sudden encounter with the shield raised under the activity's rules.
Defend.best_user: A shield user expecting immediate danger.

Detect_Magic.purpose: Repeatedly cast detect magic while traveling.
Detect_Magic.effect_summary: Notice magical auras according to the spell and exploration procedure.
Detect_Magic.best_user: A caster searching for magical hazards or objects.

Follow_the_Expert.purpose: Use an ally's expertise to attempt an exploration task.
Follow_the_Expert.effect_summary: Gain a proficiency-based benefit while following a trained or better ally.
Follow_the_Expert.best_user: A party member who is untrained or weaker at a required travel skill.

Hustle.purpose: Travel faster for a limited time.
Hustle.effect_summary: Increase overland movement according to Constitution and group pace.

Investigate.purpose: Look for clues and interpret details.
Investigate.effect_summary: Use Recall Knowledge repeatedly while moving at reduced pace.

Repeat_a_Spell.purpose: Continuously renew a spell or cantrip.
Repeat_a_Spell.effect_summary: Cast the same spell at intervals, often to maintain a short-duration utility effect.

Scout.effect_summary: Grant the party a circumstance bonus to initiative when an encounter begins, subject to the activity.

Search.purpose: Look for hidden doors, hazards, creatures, and objects.
Search.effect_summary: Use Perception as the group moves, generally at reduced pace.

Track.purpose: Follow signs of a creature's passage.
Track.effect_summary: Use Survival against a tracking DC.
Track.best_user: A ranger, scout, or wilderness expert.

group_coverage_example: Remaining character: Scout or Detect Magic
travel_questions: What is the party's marching order?
Who carries light or has darkvision?
How fast is the slowest member?
What exploration activity is each character using?
How are doors, corners, and suspicious objects approached?
How much time is available for recovery?

common_activities.Earn_Income: Use a skill to perform work over days and earn currency based on task level, proficiency, and result.
common_activities.Craft: Create or repair items using the current Crafting rules, formulas or access requirements, time, and materials.
common_activities.Retrain: Replace eligible character choices after spending the required downtime and meeting prerequisites.
common_activities.Subsist: Secure basic food and shelter when living costs are not otherwise paid.
common_activities.Treat_Disease: Use Medicine over time to assist a diseased creature.
common_activities.Long_Term_Rest: Spend a full day and night resting to regain additional HP.
common_activities.Research_or_subsystems: Published adventures and GM Core can add influence, research, reputation, organizations, and other structured downtime.

campaign_use: Downtime makes professions and Lore skills matter.
It lets characters change legal choices through retraining instead of rebuilding the entire character.
It provides a space for relationships, crafting, businesses, and personal goals.
The GM should state how many days are available and what task levels can be found.

arcane.broad_identity: Scholarly and technical magic with extensive offense, control, transformation, and utility.

divine.broad_identity: Magic connected to deities, faith, spirits, healing, protection, and sanctified powers.

occult.broad_identity: Mind, emotion, spirit, story, strange knowledge, illusion, and esoteric influence.

primal.broad_identity: Elements, life, animals, plants, weather, healing, and transformation.

spell_components_and_actions.remastered_presentation: Spell entries show action icons and traits rather than relying on the legacy verbal, somatic, and material component framework.
spell_components_and_actions.action_cost: A spell can cost 1, 2, or 3 actions, a reaction, free action, minutes, or longer as listed.
spell_components_and_actions.traits_matter: Manipulate, concentrate, attack, incapacitation, linguistic, auditory, visual, and tradition traits can change how a spell interacts with other rules.

procedure: During daily preparations, choose which spells fill available spell slots.
Casting a prepared spell expends that prepared slot.
Preparing the same spell in multiple slots allows multiple castings.
prepared_casting.planning_tip: Prepare a mix of reliable general spells and a few spells based on expected challenges.

procedure: Maintain a spell repertoire of known spells.
When casting, choose an appropriate spell from the repertoire and expend a slot of a legal rank.
Slots are flexible, but repertoire changes are limited to leveling, retraining, or specific abilities.
Signature spells and class rules govern flexible heightening.
spontaneous_casting.planning_tip: Choose spells that remain useful in many situations because known-spell slots are valuable.

cantrips.use: Can be cast repeatedly without expending spell slots.
cantrips.heightening: Automatically heighten to half the character's level rounded up unless a rule says otherwise.
cantrips.role: Provide a repeatable magical option and utility after ranked spell slots are spent.

focus_spells.normal_pool_limit: Usually no more than 3, and generally no more than the number of focus spells available, subject to class rules.
focus_spells.casting: Most focus spells cost 1 Focus Point.
focus_spells.refocus: Spend 10 minutes performing a class-appropriate activity to regain a Focus Point; current rules can allow repeated Refocus activities, subject to the exact character rules.

heightening.definition: Casting a spell at a higher rank can improve numerical effects or unlock additional effects listed in its heightened entry.
heightening.prepared: Prepare the spell in a higher-rank slot.
heightening.spontaneous: Know or qualify to cast the higher-rank version, commonly through signature-spell rules or separate repertoire entries.

targeting.range: The target or area must be within the listed range.
targeting.line_of_effect: A physical or magical barrier can block an effect even when the target is visible.
targeting.perception: A caster usually must perceive a chosen target well enough to target it.
targeting.friendly_fire: Area spells affect creatures according to their area and text; allies are not automatically excluded.

spell_attacks_and_saves.spell_attack: Roll a spell attack against AC. The attack trait means multiple attack penalty can apply.
spell_attacks_and_saves.saving_throw: The target rolls the listed save against the caster's spell DC.
spell_attacks_and_saves.basic_save: Use the standard no/half/full/double damage pattern only when the spell says the save is basic.
spell_attacks_and_saves.incapacitation: Effects with this trait are less able to fully disable targets of substantially higher level; read the trait before relying on such a spell against a boss.

sustain.summary: Some spells require the Sustain action on later turns to continue or move their effects.
sustain.turn_planning: Reserve an action for Sustain before committing the rest of the turn.

counteracting.summary: Dispel magic, counteracting conditions, and similar effects compare a counteract check and counteract rank to the target effect.
counteracting.advice: Use the full counteract rules or an updated digital reference; do not reduce the system to a simple opposed roll.

actions: Use a 1-action focus, composition, hex, or class ability
Cast a 1-action spell or use a skill action
Cast a 2-action spell selected for the discovered defense or weakness

equipment_and_bulk.item_level: Item level indicates approximate power and acquisition expectations; it is not normally a requirement to use an item unless the item says so.

rarity.common: Normally available under ordinary character creation and settlement access.
rarity.uncommon: Requires access, GM permission, or a source that grants access.
rarity.rare: Generally requires explicit campaign or GM approval.

bulk.maximum_normal_capacity: 10 + Strength modifier Bulk, subject to creature size and specific rules
bulk.light_items: Ten light items normally count as 1 Bulk.
bulk.negligible_items: Do not count individually unless carried in very large numbers.
bulk.encumbered_effect: Clumsy 1 and a 10-foot penalty to Speeds.

trait_examples.finesse: Can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack roll, but not automatically for damage.
trait_examples.deadly: Adds specified weapon dice on a critical hit.
trait_examples.fatal: Changes the weapon die and adds a die on a critical hit as specified.
trait_examples.trip: Can use the weapon for Trip with the trait's benefits.
trait_examples.versatile: Can change to a listed alternate damage type.

armor.beginner_rule: The highest item bonus is not always the best armor; proficiency, Dexterity cap, Strength, Speed, and check penalties all matter.

shields.raise: Raise a Shield grants its AC bonus until the start of the next turn.
shields.block: Shield Block is a reaction available only when granted. It reduces damage using Hardness, then the shield and wielder take remaining damage according to the reaction.
shields.maintenance: A damaged shield can be Repaired with Crafting and appropriate tools.

fundamental_runes.weapon_potency: Improves attack item bonus and enables property rune capacity.
fundamental_runes.striking: Increases the number of weapon damage dice.
fundamental_runes.armor_potency: Improves AC item bonus and enables property rune capacity.
fundamental_runes.campaign_note: The expected mathematical progression assumes access to level-appropriate fundamental bonuses unless the campaign uses an alternative-bonus system.

conditions.usage_note: Conditions are compact rules packages. Always check the full current entry when exact timing or exceptions matter.

blinded.summary: You cannot see. Normal terrain is difficult terrain to you, visual Perception checks critically fail, you are off-guard, and you need flat checks to target creatures you cannot precisely sense.
blinded.play_tip: Use another precise sense if your character has one; otherwise seek cover, remove the condition, or use effects that do not require choosing a visually perceived target.

clumsy.summary: Apply the condition value as a status penalty to Dexterity-based checks and DCs, including AC, Reflex saves, ranged attacks, and relevant skills.
clumsy.play_tip: Because it reduces AC and Reflex, remove it quickly when facing accurate attackers or area effects.

concealed.summary: A creature is difficult to see clearly. A targeted attack or effect normally requires a DC 5 flat check before resolving.
concealed.play_tip: Area effects that do not target a specific creature can often bypass this targeting check.

confused.summary: You are off-guard, do not treat anyone as an ally, cannot Delay, Ready, or use reactions, and must use your actions to attack or otherwise harm nearby creatures according to the condition.
confused.play_tip: Allies should avoid clustering around the confused creature and should end the condition quickly.

dazzled.summary: All creatures and objects are concealed from you if sight is your only precise sense.
dazzled.play_tip: Expect DC 5 flat checks for targeted attacks and effects.

deafened.summary: You cannot hear. Auditory Perception checks critically fail, and actions with the auditory trait can be disrupted or unavailable as specified.
deafened.play_tip: Use visual signals and avoid abilities that require hearing.

doomed.summary: Your dying threshold is reduced by the doomed value. Doomed usually decreases by 1 after a full night's rest.
doomed.play_tip: Doomed makes any later knockout substantially more dangerous.

drained.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to Constitution-based checks and DCs, including Fortitude saves, and reduce maximum and current HP by your level times the value.
drained.play_tip: Track both the Fortitude penalty and the HP reduction.

dying.summary: You are unconscious and at risk of death. Make recovery checks at the start of your turn; reaching dying 4 normally kills you.
dying.play_tip: Allies should heal or stabilize you before your next recovery check whenever possible.

encumbered.summary: When carried Bulk exceeds 5 plus your Strength modifier, you become clumsy 1 and take a 10-foot penalty to Speeds until reducing the load.
encumbered.play_tip: Store situational gear on a pack animal, vehicle, or in a secure location.

enfeebled.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to Strength-based checks and DCs, including most melee attacks and Athletics.
enfeebled.play_tip: Switch to Dexterity-based, spell, or support options when practical.

fascinated.summary: You take a status penalty to Perception and skill checks and cannot use actions with the concentrate trait unless they concern the subject of fascination, subject to the full condition rules.
fascinated.play_tip: Damage or hostile actions often help bring the condition to an end, depending on its source.

fatigued.summary: You take a status penalty to AC and saving throws and cannot use exploration activities performed while traveling.
fatigued.play_tip: Rest before entering a dangerous area; fatigue weakens both combat defense and exploration readiness.

fleeing.summary: On your turn, you must spend actions trying to escape the source of the condition as efficiently as possible.
fleeing.play_tip: Plan for the character to lose tactical control until the duration expires.

frightened.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to all checks and DCs. Unless specified otherwise, reduce frightened by 1 at the end of each of your turns.
frightened.play_tip: Because it lowers both offense and defense, frightened is a broadly useful debuff.

grabbed.summary: You are off-guard and immobilized. Manipulate actions require a DC 5 flat check or are disrupted.
grabbed.play_tip: Escape, forced movement, or defeating the grabbing creature can restore mobility.

hidden.summary: A creature knows your space but cannot precisely perceive you. Targeting you normally requires a DC 11 flat check.
hidden.play_tip: Seek can reduce hidden to observed; movement and cover can preserve or improve stealth.

immobilized.summary: You cannot use actions with the move trait. Forced movement can work only when it overcomes the immobilizing effect as specified.
immobilized.play_tip: Escape or remove the source before planning a movement-dependent turn.

invisible.summary: You cannot be seen. Creatures relying on sight usually treat you as undetected until they locate you, then hidden while they know your space.
invisible.play_tip: Invisible is not automatically undetectable; noise, tracks, imprecise senses, and Seek still matter.

off_guard.summary: You take a -2 circumstance penalty to AC.
off_guard.play_tip: Off-guard enables many precision and teamwork effects, including a rogue's sneak attack.

paralyzed.summary: Your body is frozen. You are off-guard and cannot act except for mental actions that the condition permits.
paralyzed.play_tip: This is an emergency condition; prioritize removal or protection.

persistent_damage.summary: At the end of each turn, take the listed damage, then attempt the normal flat check to end it. Assistance or especially effective countermeasures can improve the check.
persistent_damage.play_tip: Use actions to remove dangerous persistent damage when waiting for the normal check is too risky.

prone.summary: You are off-guard and take penalties to attacks. Standing is an action with the move trait; while prone, you can Take Cover against ranged attacks in suitable circumstances.
prone.play_tip: Standing can trigger reactions with relevant triggers, so consider Step-like alternatives, crawling, or disabling the reactor.

quickened.summary: At the start of your turn, gain one extra action that can be used only for actions named by the quickened effect.
quickened.play_tip: Mark the restricted extra action separately so it is not spent on an illegal action.

restrained.summary: You are tied up more completely than grabbed. You are off-guard, immobilized, and generally cannot use attack or manipulate actions except to Escape or Force Open restraints.
restrained.play_tip: Escaping is usually the entire immediate priority.

sickened.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to all checks and DCs. You normally cannot willingly ingest anything, and can spend an action retching to attempt a Fortitude save to reduce the value.
sickened.play_tip: Like frightened, this is a broad penalty, but it usually requires an action and save to reduce.

slowed.summary: When you regain actions at the start of your turn, reduce the number by the slowed value.
slowed.play_tip: Slowed is most painful for characters whose turns already require setup, movement, and multiple-action abilities.

stunned.summary: Lose actions equal to the stunned value when you next regain actions, then reduce stunned by the number lost. Stunned without a value prevents acting for its duration.
stunned.play_tip: Track whether the effect uses a numeric value or duration wording.

stupefied.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to Intelligence-, Wisdom-, and Charisma-based checks and DCs. Casting a spell usually also requires a flat check based on the condition.
stupefied.play_tip: Casters should consider non-spell actions until the condition is removed.

unconscious.summary: You cannot act, are off-guard, and take perception-related penalties. Waking depends on the cause, such as sleep, being knocked out, or another effect.
unconscious.play_tip: A creature at 0 HP also follows the dying rules unless an exception applies.

undetected.summary: A creature does not know which space you occupy. It can choose a space to target, but the GM resolves whether the guess and required flat check succeed.
undetected.play_tip: Seek, sound, tracks, and area effects are common counters.

wounded.summary: If you begin dying again, add the wounded value to the dying value you gain. Wounded usually ends after successful Treat Wounds that restores HP, or after being restored to full HP and resting for 10 minutes.
wounded.play_tip: Repeated knockouts become increasingly dangerous; heal and clear wounded before the next difficult fight.

standard_xp.carryover: XP beyond the threshold carries toward the next level.
standard_xp.milestone_option: The GM can level the party at story milestones instead of tracking XP.

what_changes_at_level_up: Increase maximum HP by the class's per-level amount plus the applicable Constitution contribution.
Increase every proficiency bonus that includes level by 1 automatically.
Gain class features listed at the new level.
Select feats, skill increases, spells, or other options granted at the new level.
Recalculate attacks, AC, saves, Perception, skills, class DC, spell DC, and item interactions.
Check whether prerequisites are now met.
Update character wealth and equipment goals.

common_progression_landmarks.every_level: Class progression and level-based proficiency increase.
common_progression_landmarks.skill_feats: Usually gained at even levels, with class exceptions such as rogue and investigator.
common_progression_landmarks.class_feats: Usually gained at even levels, plus any class-specific grants.
common_progression_landmarks.general_feats: Commonly gained at 3rd level and every 4 levels thereafter.
common_progression_landmarks.attribute_boosts: Four boosts at 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter.
common_progression_landmarks.skill_increases: Expert becomes available at 3rd, master at 7th, and legendary at 15th, subject to class progression.

advancement.retraining: Eligible feats, skills, spells, and class choices can often be changed through downtime. Some foundational choices cannot be retrained without special permission.

accuracy_and_critical_hits: Because a result 10 over the DC is a critical success, every +1 can improve both hit chance and critical chance.
Penalties to enemy AC can be as valuable as bonuses to ally attacks.
Combine off-guard, frightened, status bonuses, item bonuses, and circumstance bonuses when their types legally stack.
A boss with higher defenses often requires coordinated setup rather than repeated unsupported attacks.
action_economy: Spend actions to deny enemy actions: moving away can force an enemy to Stride.
Use Step when a movement-triggered reaction is dangerous.
Avoid a third attack unless its expected value is still worthwhile.
One-action support abilities are powerful because they fit beside a two-action spell or activity.
Ready and Delay alter timing but have meaningful opportunity costs.
defense: Raise a Shield, Take Cover, Step away, or impose conditions instead of assuming offense is always optimal.
Spread out when facing likely area effects.
Protect wounded allies from another knockout.
Remember that frightened or sickened lowers your DCs as well as checks.
Use terrain and doorways to control how many enemies can attack at once.
boss_fight_plan: Recall Knowledge to identify defenses, weaknesses, reactions, and signature threats.
Apply a legal status penalty such as frightened.
Create off-guard through flanking, Trip, Feint, or another ability.
Attack with the party's most accurate or damaging actions after setup.
Preserve escape, healing, and defensive actions.
low_level_survival: Low-level critical hits can be dangerous.
Do not split the party during hostile exploration without accepting the risk.
Treat Wounds and Refocus after difficult encounters when time permits.
Retreat is a valid tactical decision.
beginner_tactics.editorial_note: This section is practical strategy advice derived from the rules, not mandatory procedure.

minimum_preparation: Know the opening situation and the player characters' reason to engage.
Prepare two or three locations and several flexible NPC motivations.
Use published creature and hazard statistics rather than improvising all numbers.
Record likely DCs, treasure, clues, and encounter goals.
Prepare what happens if the party fails, avoids combat, negotiates, or retreats.
Have the conditions and basic actions reference available.
running_checks: Do not call for a roll when success is automatic, failure has no meaningful consequence, or repetition would eventually guarantee success without cost.
State what the player perceives and ask what they do.
Choose the relevant check and DC.
Decide whether the check is public or secret.
Apply all four degrees of success when the action provides them.
Describe the fictional result, not only the number.

preferred_order: Use the DC printed in the action, creature, hazard, spell, or adventure.
Use a simple DC based on required proficiency for ordinary tasks.
Use a level-based DC for level-scaled creatures, hazards, items, and challenges.
Apply difficulty adjustments for unusually easy or hard circumstances.
setting_dcs.warning: Do not raise every DC merely because a character is specialized; specialization should produce reliable success in that character's field.

encounter_operation: Establish positions, visibility, detection, and terrain before initiative.
Ask what exploration activity each character was using.
Roll initiative with Perception or an approach-appropriate skill.
State creature actions clearly and apply traits.
Track multiple attack penalty separately for each creature's turn.
Announce observable conditions and damage while preserving hidden information.
End the encounter when opposition is defeated, flees, surrenders, or the objective is resolved.
encounter_design_principles: Use GM Core encounter budgets and creature levels.
One higher-level enemy often feels different from several lower-level enemies because defenses affect critical rates.
Mix objectives, terrain, hazards, and enemy behavior instead of relying only on reducing HP.
Avoid stacking multiple severe encounters without recovery unless the danger is intentional and communicated.
Reward scouting and negotiation by allowing them to change position, information, or encounter difficulty.
adjudication_principles: Traits are rules and should be checked.
A ruling should be consistent, fair, and reversible after the session if research shows an error.
Do not secretly remove a character's core ability merely because it solves a prepared obstacle.
When uncertain, choose a temporary ruling, record the question, and verify later.

first_session_walkthrough.premise: The party escorts a scholar to an abandoned watchtower where livestock have vanished.

scene_1_social.gm_prompt: A frightened shepherd blocks the road and insists the tower is cursed.
possible_player_actions: Diplomacy to Make an Impression or Request details
Religion, Occultism, or local Lore to interpret the curse story
Perception to notice what the shepherd is hiding
scene_1_social.teaching_goal: Show that players choose approaches and that different skills change consequences.

scene_2_exploration.gm_prompt: The trail enters dense brush and old stone ruins.
scene_2_exploration.teaching_goal: Assign exploration activities and establish marching order before danger.

scene_3_hazard.gm_prompt: A sagging floor conceals an old pit.
resolution_example: The searching character may receive a secret Perception check.
Once found, the party can go around, Disable a Device, bridge it, jump, or deliberately trigger it safely.
Use degrees of success and consequences rather than forcing one solution.
scene_3_hazard.teaching_goal: Demonstrate hidden information, hazards, and creative problem solving.

scene_4_encounter.opposition: A small group of level-appropriate scavenging creatures.
start: Prompt players with basic actions without choosing for them.
sample_team_turn: Fighter Strides, Strikes, and Raises a Shield.
Rogue moves to flank and Strikes the off-guard enemy.
Cleric uses a support spell and moves to safety.
Wizard Recalls Knowledge, then casts a spell aimed at the weaker defense.
scene_4_encounter.teaching_goal: Show action flexibility, off-guard, multiple attack penalty, spells, and teamwork.

scene_5_recovery.teaching_goal: Teach that recovery and exploration are part of the adventure loop.

scene_6_choice.reveal: The supposed monster is protecting eggs from a more dangerous intruder.
scene_6_choice.teaching_goal: Reinforce that encounters are objectives and decisions, not mandatory fights.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Treating a natural 20 as always a critical success.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: First compare the total with the DC, then improve the degree by one step.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Adding two status bonuses or two circumstance bonuses.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Same-type bonuses do not stack; use the highest.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting that Trip, Grapple, Escape, and spell attacks can increase multiple attack penalty.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Check for the attack trait, not only whether the action is called Strike.
The second and third attacks are penalized; use movement, defense, skills, or support when they provide more value.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Assuming every character has Reactive Strike.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Movement and manipulate actions trigger reactions only when a creature actually has a reaction with that trigger.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Treating Raise a Shield and Shield Block as the same action.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Raise a Shield improves AC; Shield Block is a separate reaction requiring access.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting off-guard affects AC, not every defense.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Off-guard is a -2 circumstance penalty to AC.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Applying multiple attack penalty to saving-throw spells.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: It applies to actions with the attack trait; a spell that only calls for a save normally does not increase it.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Assuming spell rank equals character level.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Cantrip and spell-rank progression uses roughly half character level, and class tables show slots.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Ignoring line of effect because the target is visible.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: A transparent or visible barrier can still block an effect.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Using legacy flat-footed terminology in a remastered game.
Starting every encounter at low HP because healing is considered optional.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Parties are expected to use available recovery; encounter difficulty can rise sharply when entering injured.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting wounded when a character is knocked out again.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Add wounded to the dying value gained.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Letting players see all secret Recall Knowledge or Search rolls.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Use secret checks when knowing the die would reveal whether information is reliable.

common_rules_mistakes.mistake: Assuming uncommon means stronger than common.
common_rules_mistakes.correction: Rarity primarily controls access and setting assumptions, not a universal power increase.
A functioning character also needs defenses, movement, exploration contribution, and useful actions when attacking is poor.

terms.note: Remastered creation and advancement generally work directly with modifiers rather than separate scores.
The mechanical AC penalty remains the central effect.
This avoids confusing spell progression with character level.
It remains a specific reaction, not a universal ability.
Use the current trait and effect text for living and undead interactions.
Use the current trait and effect text for living and undead interactions.

terms.remastered: spirit damage, holy/unholy sanctification, edicts, anathema, and specific traits

terms.legacy: traditional eight universal schools of magic
terms.remastered: spell traits plus wizard curriculum schools

terms.legacy: material, somatic, and verbal components as the main spell presentation
terms.remastered: action icons and traits such as manipulate and concentrate
terms.note: Use each remastered spell's listed actions and traits.
Ancestry combines with heritage and ancestry feats.

compatibility_procedure: Look for a remastered version of the option first.
Use the remastered version when both versions represent the same option.
Check official errata and compatibility guidance.
Ask the GM before using an option with removed alignment, school, or damage concepts.
Document the table's final conversion so it stays consistent.

quick_reference.standard_cover: +2 circumstance bonus to AC, area Reflex, and Stealth to Hide
quick_reference.step: move 5 feet without triggering movement reactions
quick_reference.raise_shield: gain shield AC bonus until next turn
quick_reference.hero_point_reroll: spend 1 and use the new result
quick_reference.heroic_recovery: spend all Hero Points, at least 1, to lose dying without gaining wounded

glossary.action: A unit of effort spent during a turn.
glossary.activity: A task that uses two or more actions, or a longer amount of time, and must normally be completed as a unit.
glossary.ancestry: A character's people or lineage, combined with a heritage and ancestry feats.
glossary.archetype: A feat-based package that expands a character through a dedication and follow-up feats.
glossary.armor_class: The DC an attack roll must meet to hit.
glossary.attribute: One of Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma.
glossary.bonus: A positive modifier, often typed as circumstance, item, or status.
glossary.bulk: An abstraction for item weight, size, and carrying difficulty.
glossary.cantrip: A reusable spell that automatically heightens.
glossary.class_dc: A DC used by certain class abilities.
glossary.critical_specialization: An additional effect available on a critical weapon hit when a rule grants access.
glossary.dc: Difficulty Class; the target number a check must meet.
glossary.degree_of_success: Critical success, success, failure, or critical failure.
glossary.downtime: The mode for activities measured in days or longer.
glossary.encounter: The mode for precise rounds and initiative.
glossary.exploration: The mode for travel and activities measured in minutes or hours.
glossary.feat: A selected ability that customizes ancestry, class, skills, or general capabilities.
glossary.flat_check: An unmodified d20 roll against a flat DC.
glossary.focus_point: A renewable resource used for focus spells.
glossary.fortune: A trait for effects that beneficially alter how a roll is made.
glossary.free_action: An action that costs no normal action but can have a trigger or timing.
glossary.heritage: A specific expression of an ancestry.
glossary.hero_point: A session-based resource used for a reroll or Heroic Recovery.
glossary.initiative: The order in which participants take turns in encounter mode.
glossary.level: A measure of character, creature, hazard, item, or challenge power.
glossary.multiple_attack_penalty: The penalty applied to later attack-trait actions on the same turn.
glossary.penalty: A negative modifier, often typed as circumstance, item, or status.
glossary.perception: Awareness used for sensing and usually initiative.
glossary.proficiency: Training rank: untrained, trained, expert, master, or legendary.
glossary.reaction: An action used when its trigger occurs.
glossary.repertoire: The spells a spontaneous caster knows and can select when casting.
glossary.round: A cycle in which each encounter participant normally takes one turn; about 6 seconds.
glossary.saving_throw: Fortitude, Reflex, or Will defense check.
glossary.secret_check: A check rolled by the GM to preserve uncertainty.
glossary.spell_rank: The power category of a spell, distinct from character level.
glossary.status_bonus: A typed bonus usually created by magic, morale, or a condition.
glossary.strike: The basic weapon or unarmed attack action.
glossary.trait: A rules-bearing tag that classifies and modifies an option.
glossary.trigger: The event that permits a reaction or triggered free action.
glossary.turn: One participant's opportunity to act in initiative.
glossary.weakness: Extra damage or effect applied when the named type affects a creature.

before_session_1: Read the thirty-second summary and core resolution system.
Learn the character's attack, AC, saves, Perception, and five most-used actions.
Mark which actions have the attack, manipulate, concentrate, or move traits.
during_session_1: Say what the character wants before naming a rule.
Ask what is visible, how far away targets are, and what cover exists.
Use one accurate attack and one non-attack action during early rounds.
Record unresolved rules questions instead of stopping every scene.
after_session_1: Choose two new tactical combinations with allies.
Read only the conditions, skill actions, and spell rules that actually appeared.
Retrain later if a legal choice is not enjoyable.
sessions_2_to_5: Learn Recall Knowledge and one combat maneuver.
Practice Delay, Ready, and reaction timing.
Use cover, concealment, and detection rules.
Learn dying and wounded rules before the first serious emergency.

redistribution_guidance: Do not present editorial complexity ratings or recommendations as official Paizo classifications.

Before publishing a commercial or derivative implementation, review the current Pathfinder compatibility, ORC, Community Use, and product-identity requirements that apply to the material actually used.
Names and short factual statistics can be indexed, but avoid copying full protected expression from rulebooks or reference pages.

categories.ancestry_feat: Expresses ancestry, heritage, culture, physiology, or inherited magic; normally selected at levels 1, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
categories.class_feat: Customizes class tactics and subsystems; most classes gain these at even levels and often at level 1.
categories.skill_feat: Expands a trained or better skill; most characters gain one at even levels.
categories.general_feat: Broad capability; commonly gained at levels 3, 7, 11, 15, and 19.
categories.archetype_feat: Begins with a dedication and replaces a feat of the permitted category; dedication restrictions govern taking another dedication.
categories.mythic_feat: Used only when the campaign uses mythic rules.

validation: Character level must meet or exceed feat level.
All prerequisites, access requirements, rarity permissions, and trait restrictions must be satisfied.
A skill feat requires the listed skill proficiency.
An archetype dedication can restrict taking another dedication until enough feats from the archetype are selected.
A feat cannot be selected twice unless it explicitly allows repetition.
Remastered and legacy versions with the same identity should not be combined as separate benefits.

animal_companions.core_rule_summary: A minion normally receives 2 actions when its controller uses the action required to command it. Mature and specialized companions can alter this economy.

familiars.core_rule_summary: Choose familiar and master abilities during daily preparations as permitted. Familiar statistics derive from the master under the familiar rules rather than using an ordinary creature stat block.

eidolons.core_rule_summary: A summoner and eidolon share Hit Points and a four-action turn framework, but remain separate creatures for positioning and many effects. Use the exact Act Together and shared-HP rules.

deity_and_belief_framework.selection_rule: Characters can hold beliefs without receiving mechanical deity benefits. Clerics and champions must satisfy their class's exact deity and sanctification requirements.
deity_and_belief_framework.remaster_note: Use edicts, anathema, sanctification, holy/unholy traits, and spirit damage rather than the removed universal alignment framework.

attribute_boost_engine.boost_at_plus_4_or_higher: A boost becomes a partial boost; two partial boosts are required for the next +1.
attribute_boost_engine.ancestry_alternative: Where permitted, replace listed ancestry boosts and flaw with two free boosts.
attribute_boost_engine.free_boost_constraint: Within one set of four free boosts, choose four different attributes.
attribute_boost_engine.normal_level_1_ceiling: A standard 1st-level character generally begins with no attribute above +4.

proficiency_engine.same_type_stacking: Use only the highest bonus and worst penalty of each typed category.
