blinded.summary: You cannot see. Normal terrain is difficult terrain to you, visual Perception checks critically fail, you are off-guard, and you need flat checks to target creatures you cannot precisely sense.
blinded.play_tip: Use another precise sense if your character has one; otherwise seek cover, remove the condition, or use effects that do not require choosing a visually perceived target.

clumsy.summary: Apply the condition value as a status penalty to Dexterity-based checks and DCs, including AC, Reflex saves, ranged attacks, and relevant skills.
clumsy.play_tip: Because it reduces AC and Reflex, remove it quickly when facing accurate attackers or area effects.

concealed.summary: A creature is difficult to see clearly. A targeted attack or effect normally requires a DC 5 flat check before resolving.
concealed.play_tip: Area effects that do not target a specific creature can often bypass this targeting check.

confused.summary: You are off-guard, do not treat anyone as an ally, cannot Delay, Ready, or use reactions, and must use your actions to attack or otherwise harm nearby creatures according to the condition.
confused.play_tip: Allies should avoid clustering around the confused creature and should end the condition quickly.

dazzled.summary: All creatures and objects are concealed from you if sight is your only precise sense.
dazzled.play_tip: Expect DC 5 flat checks for targeted attacks and effects.

deafened.summary: You cannot hear. Auditory Perception checks critically fail, and actions with the auditory trait can be disrupted or unavailable as specified.
deafened.play_tip: Use visual signals and avoid abilities that require hearing.

doomed.summary: Your dying threshold is reduced by the doomed value. Doomed usually decreases by 1 after a full night's rest.
doomed.play_tip: Doomed makes any later knockout substantially more dangerous.

drained.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to Constitution-based checks and DCs, including Fortitude saves, and reduce maximum and current HP by your level times the value.
drained.play_tip: Track both the Fortitude penalty and the HP reduction.

dying.summary: You are unconscious and at risk of death. Make recovery checks at the start of your turn; reaching dying 4 normally kills you.
dying.play_tip: Allies should heal or stabilize you before your next recovery check whenever possible.

encumbered.summary: When carried Bulk exceeds 5 plus your Strength modifier, you become clumsy 1 and take a 10-foot penalty to Speeds until reducing the load.
encumbered.play_tip: Store situational gear on a pack animal, vehicle, or in a secure location.

enfeebled.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to Strength-based checks and DCs, including most melee attacks and Athletics.
enfeebled.play_tip: Switch to Dexterity-based, spell, or support options when practical.

fascinated.summary: You take a status penalty to Perception and skill checks and cannot use actions with the concentrate trait unless they concern the subject of fascination, subject to the full condition rules.
fascinated.play_tip: Damage or hostile actions often help bring the condition to an end, depending on its source.

fatigued.summary: You take a status penalty to AC and saving throws and cannot use exploration activities performed while traveling.
fatigued.play_tip: Rest before entering a dangerous area; fatigue weakens both combat defense and exploration readiness.

fleeing.summary: On your turn, you must spend actions trying to escape the source of the condition as efficiently as possible.
fleeing.play_tip: Plan for the character to lose tactical control until the duration expires.

frightened.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to all checks and DCs. Unless specified otherwise, reduce frightened by 1 at the end of each of your turns.
frightened.play_tip: Because it lowers both offense and defense, frightened is a broadly useful debuff.

grabbed.summary: You are off-guard and immobilized. Manipulate actions require a DC 5 flat check or are disrupted.
grabbed.play_tip: Escape, forced movement, or defeating the grabbing creature can restore mobility.

hidden.summary: A creature knows your space but cannot precisely perceive you. Targeting you normally requires a DC 11 flat check.
hidden.play_tip: Seek can reduce hidden to observed; movement and cover can preserve or improve stealth.

immobilized.summary: You cannot use actions with the move trait. Forced movement can work only when it overcomes the immobilizing effect as specified.
immobilized.play_tip: Escape or remove the source before planning a movement-dependent turn.

invisible.summary: You cannot be seen. Creatures relying on sight usually treat you as undetected until they locate you, then hidden while they know your space.
invisible.play_tip: Invisible is not automatically undetectable; noise, tracks, imprecise senses, and Seek still matter.

off_guard.summary: You take a -2 circumstance penalty to AC.
off_guard.play_tip: Off-guard enables many precision and teamwork effects, including a rogue's sneak attack.

paralyzed.summary: Your body is frozen. You are off-guard and cannot act except for mental actions that the condition permits.
paralyzed.play_tip: This is an emergency condition; prioritize removal or protection.

persistent_damage.summary: At the end of each turn, take the listed damage, then attempt the normal flat check to end it. Assistance or especially effective countermeasures can improve the check.
persistent_damage.play_tip: Use actions to remove dangerous persistent damage when waiting for the normal check is too risky.

prone.summary: You are off-guard and take penalties to attacks. Standing is an action with the move trait; while prone, you can Take Cover against ranged attacks in suitable circumstances.
prone.play_tip: Standing can trigger reactions with relevant triggers, so consider Step-like alternatives, crawling, or disabling the reactor.

quickened.summary: At the start of your turn, gain one extra action that can be used only for actions named by the quickened effect.
quickened.play_tip: Mark the restricted extra action separately so it is not spent on an illegal action.

restrained.summary: You are tied up more completely than grabbed. You are off-guard, immobilized, and generally cannot use attack or manipulate actions except to Escape or Force Open restraints.
restrained.play_tip: Escaping is usually the entire immediate priority.

sickened.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to all checks and DCs. You normally cannot willingly ingest anything, and can spend an action retching to attempt a Fortitude save to reduce the value.
sickened.play_tip: Like frightened, this is a broad penalty, but it usually requires an action and save to reduce.

slowed.summary: When you regain actions at the start of your turn, reduce the number by the slowed value.
slowed.play_tip: Slowed is most painful for characters whose turns already require setup, movement, and multiple-action abilities.

stunned.summary: Lose actions equal to the stunned value when you next regain actions, then reduce stunned by the number lost. Stunned without a value prevents acting for its duration.
stunned.play_tip: Track whether the effect uses a numeric value or duration wording.

stupefied.summary: Apply the value as a status penalty to Intelligence-, Wisdom-, and Charisma-based checks and DCs. Casting a spell usually also requires a flat check based on the condition.
stupefied.play_tip: Casters should consider non-spell actions until the condition is removed.

unconscious.summary: You cannot act, are off-guard, and take perception-related penalties. Waking depends on the cause, such as sleep, being knocked out, or another effect.
unconscious.play_tip: A creature at 0 HP also follows the dying rules unless an exception applies.

undetected.summary: A creature does not know which space you occupy. It can choose a space to target, but the GM resolves whether the guess and required flat check succeed.
undetected.play_tip: Seek, sound, tracks, and area effects are common counters.

wounded.summary: If you begin dying again, add the wounded value to the dying value you gain. Wounded usually ends after successful Treat Wounds that restores HP, or after being restored to full HP and resting for 10 minutes.
wounded.play_tip: Repeated knockouts become increasingly dangerous; heal and clear wounded before the next difficult fight.

broken.summary: An item at or below its Broken Threshold cannot be used normally and imposes the limitations in the broken condition; repair it before further use.
broken.play_tip: Track shield HP and Broken Threshold separately.

controlled.summary: Another creature determines your actions, subject to the controlling effect. You usually cannot choose actions against the controller's directions.
controlled.play_tip: Protection and condition removal are urgent because the player loses tactical agency.

cursebound.summary: An oracle-only valued condition increased by cursebound abilities. The chosen mystery determines its drawbacks, and Refocus removes it.
cursebound.play_tip: Record current and maximum cursebound values visibly.

friendly.summary: An attitude condition: the creature is favorably disposed and may accept reasonable Requests.
friendly.play_tip: Friendly is not obedience; motives and risk still matter.

helpful.summary: An attitude condition: the creature is willing to assist, within its capabilities and interests.
helpful.play_tip: Even helpful creatures can refuse extreme sacrifice.

hostile.summary: An attitude condition: the creature actively seeks to harm or oppose you.
hostile.play_tip: Changing attitude may require leverage, withdrawal, or a longer social approach.

indifferent.summary: An attitude condition: the creature has no strong view and normally needs a reason to help.
indifferent.play_tip: Make an Impression before making significant Requests.

observed.summary: A detection state in which a creature is clearly perceived by a precise sense.
observed.play_tip: Observed creatures can normally be targeted without a concealment or hidden flat check.

unfriendly.summary: An attitude condition: the creature dislikes or distrusts you and is unlikely to help without a strong reason.
unfriendly.play_tip: Avoid treating a single Diplomacy check as mind control.

unnoticed.summary: A detection state in which a creature does not know you are present at all.
unnoticed.play_tip: An action that reveals presence can shift unnoticed to undetected, hidden, or observed.

value_rules: A valued condition uses its number wherever the condition says.
Do not add two instances unless the condition says to; usually use the higher value or modify the existing value.
Durations, recovery, and removal methods belong to the effect that imposed the condition or the condition entry.
Attitudes and detection states are rules terms even though they function differently from numerical penalties.

detection_and_senses.concealed: The observer knows and sees the target indistinctly; targeted effects normally require DC 5 flat check.
detection_and_senses.hidden: The observer knows the target's space but cannot precisely perceive it; targeted effects normally require DC 11 flat check.
detection_and_senses.undetected: The observer does not know the target's exact space; choose or guess a space and then resolve targeting.
detection_and_senses.unnoticed: The observer is unaware the target is present.
detection_and_senses.precise_sense: Can make a creature observed under normal conditions.
detection_and_senses.imprecise_sense: Can locate a creature's space but normally only makes it hidden.
detection_and_senses.vague_sense: Can indicate presence but not location.
detection_and_senses.seek_progression: A successful Seek can improve a target from undetected to hidden or hidden to observed as the exact rules allow.

weakness_resistance_immunity_order: Determine all damage types and amounts.
Apply each applicable weakness and resistance according to current simultaneous-damage rules and errata.
Apply remaining damage to temporary HP, then current HP.
persistent_damage: Take it at end of turn.
Attempt the normal flat check to end it.
Assistance or an especially effective action can lower the DC or allow an extra check.
Multiple instances of the same type normally use the highest, not the sum.
affliction_sequence: On exposure, attempt the initial save if the affliction calls for one.
On failure, apply the listed onset and stage.
At each interval, attempt the next save.
Successes and failures move the stage as specified.
Reaching stage 0 ends the affliction unless it can expose the creature again.

selection_algorithm: Use a printed DC from the action, creature, item, hazard, spell, or adventure when available.
Use a simple DC when the task primarily asks whether a character has a proficiency tier.
Use a level-based DC when the challenge has a meaningful level.
Apply one difficulty adjustment only when circumstances genuinely differ from the baseline.
Do not scale ordinary doors, facts, and routine tasks upward solely because the party leveled.

encounter_builder.baseline_party: 4 characters of the encounter's party level

trivial.description: Little threat; useful for tone, demonstration, or resource-light opposition.

low.description: Some danger but normally manageable with sound play.

moderate.description: A meaningful challenge expected to require tactics and some resources.

severe.description: A serious threat with a real chance of character defeat or death.

extreme.description: Roughly even odds for a fully prepared party; reserve for climactic or explicitly lethal situations.

construction_algorithm: Choose intended threat level and start with its XP budget.
For each player above or below four, add or subtract the listed adjustment.
Choose creatures; each costs XP based on creature level minus party level.
Include hazards using simple or complex hazard XP.
Check action economy, terrain, range, mobility, resistances, and hard counters rather than trusting budget alone.
Reassess if one creature is party level +3 or +4, if the party cannot exploit its weaknesses, or if the encounter prevents recovery.
boss_guidance: A single higher-level creature has better AC, saves, attack modifiers, and critical rates.
Solo bosses often need terrain, objectives, minions, or phases for dynamic play, but extra enemy actions increase danger.
Do not rely on incapacitation effects against a higher-level boss without understanding the trait.
encounter_builder.party_size_formula: adjusted budget = base threat budget + (party size - 4) × threat adjustment
encounter_builder.xp_award: Award the encounter's creature and hazard XP using their relative levels; story accomplishments can add separate XP.

hazard_engine.simple_hazard: Usually resolves once or over a short sequence and grants one-fifth of comparable creature XP.
hazard_engine.complex_hazard: Operates in initiative with routines and grants XP comparable to a creature of its level.

treasure_and_item_progression.fundamental_assumption: Standard encounter math expects characters to receive level-appropriate item bonuses and weapon or armor damage progression unless the campaign uses an alternative such as Automatic Bonus Progression.
treasure_distribution_questions: Does each weapon user have an appropriate potency and striking path?
Do defenses receive armor potency and resilient improvements?
Do spellcasters receive staves, wands, scrolls, and skill items rather than only weapons?
Does treasure include consumables, utility, and story items?
Can unwanted permanent items be sold, transferred, or converted?
treasure_and_item_progression.rarity_and_access: Settlement level, item rarity, formulas, campaign access, and Game Master permission all affect availability.

turn_start: apply slowed, stunned, quickened, or other action changes

recall_knowledge_adjudication.best_practice: Answer useful questions that change decisions, not merely the creature's name.
recall_knowledge_adjudication.skill_selection: Use the skill appropriate to the subject; a narrow Lore can justify an easier DC.
recall_knowledge_adjudication.repeated_attempts: Further questions or retries can use harder DCs or become unavailable as the exact rule and situation dictate.
recall_knowledge_adjudication.secret_check: The Game Master normally rolls to preserve uncertainty.

subsystem_framework.victory_points: Track accumulated successes toward thresholds for research, influence, infiltration, chases, reputation, or other multi-scene goals.
subsystem_framework.influence: Discover NPC interests and objections, then use appropriate skills to earn influence within a limited time.
subsystem_framework.research: Use libraries or information sources with thresholds and skills to uncover progressively deeper facts.
subsystem_framework.chases: Move through obstacles using varied checks; failure costs progress or time rather than ending the scene immediately.
subsystem_framework.reputation: Track standing with factions and unlock consequences at thresholds.
subsystem_framework.hexploration: Divide wilderness into hexes and assign travel, reconnoitering, mapping, and exploration activities.
subsystem_framework.duels_and_leadership: Use only when campaign tone supports their specialized assumptions.

free_archetype.summary: Grants additional archetype feats at specified levels without replacing normal class feats.
free_archetype.impact: Raises breadth and complexity more than raw numerical bonuses; establish dedication restrictions and allowed archetypes.

automatic_bonus_progression.summary: Replaces many mandatory item bonuses and fundamental runes with automatic character bonuses.
automatic_bonus_progression.impact: Reprice or remove redundant item bonuses and follow the complete variant table.

proficiency_without_level.summary: Removes level from most proficiency calculations.
proficiency_without_level.impact: Changes encounter range, DCs, creature usability, and critical rates; apply the entire variant consistently.

gradual_attribute_boosts.summary: Distributes the four boosts normally gained every five levels across intervening levels.
gradual_attribute_boosts.impact: Track which four different attributes belong to each five-level set.

ancestry_paragon.impact: Increases ancestry expression and option count.

dual_class.impact: Major power and complexity increase; requires encounter and party-role reconsideration.

stamina.summary: Divides durability into Stamina and Hit Points with Resolve-based recovery.

avoid: single mandatory clue behind one roll
encounters whose only goal is kill everything
frequent rules overrides that negate character specialties

spell_reference_database.description_policy: Rules procedures and selection guidance are embedded. Individual spell names can be indexed by a separate licensed data source, but full proprietary spell descriptions are intentionally not copied here.

common_gaps: some direct area and utility options are narrower
some mental and institutional utility is narrower

prepared: Choose exact spells for slots during daily preparations.
Preparing the same spell more than once permits multiple casts unless the class has another system.
A spellbook, familiar, list, formula, or deity can constrain available preparation.
spontaneous: Choose a spell repertoire known over multiple levels.
Spend a suitable slot to cast a known spell.
Signature spell rules govern flexible heightening.
Repertoire errors have longer consequences, so prioritize broadly useful selections.

repeatable_baseline: one or more attack or save cantrips
a skill or weapon action for turns when magic is poor

casting_checklist: Confirm actions, trigger, range, target, line of sight, and line of effect.
Confirm whether the effect uses a spell attack or target saving throw.
Apply multiple attack penalty if the spell has the attack trait.
Check whether the target is concealed, hidden, undetected, immune, or outside the area.
Check incapacitation before using a disabling spell on a higher-level creature.
Mark the expended slot or Focus Point.
Record duration, Sustain requirement, persistent damage, and conditions.
Apply heightening from the slot or cantrip rank.

counteract_engine.counteract_modifier: Use the modifier specified by the counteracting effect, commonly spellcasting modifier or a skill.
counteract_engine.counteract_dc: Use the target effect's DC, creator DC, or listed DC.
counteract_engine.degree_and_rank: The check's degree determines the maximum target rank that can be counteracted relative to the counteract rank.
counteract_engine.warning: Use the full current counteract table for exact rank differences; do not resolve it as a simple equal-rank contest.

focus_magic.use: Most focus spells cost 1 Focus Point.
focus_magic.refocus: Spend 10 minutes in a class-appropriate activity to regain Focus Points under current rules.
focus_magic.planning: Treat Focus Points as encounter-scale renewable resources rather than hoarding them like top-rank spell slots.

staves_wands_scrolls.staff: Invest during daily preparations and use staff charges plus spellcasting access under the staff rules.
staves_wands_scrolls.wand: Normally casts its spell once per day safely; overcharging risks destruction.
staves_wands_scrolls.scroll: Consumable casting of one spell; the caster must satisfy tradition and activation rules.
staves_wands_scrolls.spellheart_and_grimoire: Use exact item rules; these can add cantrips, spell effects, or preparation benefits.

compatibility_and_versioning.baseline: Pathfinder Second Edition Remastered plus official errata through Spring 2026.
legacy_policy: Prefer the remastered version when an option has both remastered and legacy versions.
Do not gain both versions of what is substantively the same option.
Translate replaced terms such as flat-footed to off-guard, spell level to spell rank, positive/negative to vitality/void, and alignment damage to current spirit or sanctification rules.
Legacy classes and options that have not received full remastered replacements require Game Master review for removed spell schools, alignment, components, and renamed spells.
Record every table conversion in campaign notes.
source_precedence: Newest remastered printing or official rules page.
Temporary Game Master ruling documented for later review.
data_refresh_procedure: Check Paizo's FAQ and errata page.
Check Archives of Nethys current class, ancestry, spell, feat, and item indexes.
Update verified_through and source access dates.
Run schema, duplicate-ID, URL, count, and cross-index validation.

known_limits: The complete live catalogs of backgrounds, feats, archetypes, spells, equipment, creatures, and deities are linked rather than frozen into this file.
Most non-core ancestry records intentionally require a live mechanics lookup.
Class feature progression must be checked against the exact class page and current errata.
Editorial complexity ratings and tactical advice are not official Paizo classifications.
Future errata or releases can change names, rarity, mechanics, and catalog counts.

weapon_traits.agile: Use reduced multiple attack penalties: normally -4 on the second attack and -8 on later attacks.
weapon_traits.backswing: A miss can improve the next attack with that weapon on the same turn as specified.
weapon_traits.backstabber: Deals extra precision damage to off-guard targets with appropriate potency.
weapon_traits.brace: Ready the weapon against an approaching creature to gain the listed damage benefit.
weapon_traits.capacity: A multi-chamber firearm can be advanced between chambers without a full reload under the trait rules.
weapon_traits.concealable: Easier to hide on your person.
weapon_traits.deadly: On a critical hit, add the listed weapon damage dice after doubling normal damage.
weapon_traits.disarm: Can be used for Disarm and can provide the trait's item-bonus benefits.
weapon_traits.fatal: On a critical hit, increase the weapon damage die to the listed size and add an extra die after doubling.
weapon_traits.fatal_aim: Can switch between one- and two-handed use; fatal applies in the required grip.
weapon_traits.finesse: Use Dexterity instead of Strength for attack rolls; this does not automatically change damage.
weapon_traits.forceful: Later attacks on the turn deal increasing circumstance damage if they hit.
weapon_traits.free_hand: The hand remains available for many actions even while wielding the weapon, subject to trait limits.
weapon_traits.grapple: Can be used for Grapple and can provide item-bonus benefits.
weapon_traits.jousting: Mounted use changes handedness or damage as specified.
weapon_traits.modular: Interact to switch among the listed damage types.
weapon_traits.nonlethal: Can knock creatures out without the normal penalty; lethal use takes the specified penalty.
weapon_traits.parry: Spend an action to gain a circumstance bonus to AC with the weapon.
weapon_traits.propulsive: Add part of Strength modifier to ranged damage as specified.
weapon_traits.range: The listed number is the range increment; attacks beyond it take increment penalties up to the maximum.
weapon_traits.reach: Can attack creatures at the listed greater reach.
weapon_traits.reload: The listed number is the actions needed to ready the weapon for another shot, subject to special reloads.
weapon_traits.repeating: Uses a magazine; loading the magazine and individual reload behavior follow the trait.
weapon_traits.shove: Can be used for Shove and can provide item-bonus benefits.
weapon_traits.sweep: Gain a circumstance bonus when attacking a different target after a prior attack on the same turn.
weapon_traits.thrown: Use a ranged Strike with the weapon; add Strength to damage unless a rule changes it.
weapon_traits.trip: Can be used for Trip and can provide item-bonus benefits.
weapon_traits.twin: Gain extra damage when alternating attacks between paired weapons with this trait.
weapon_traits.two_hand: Wielding in two hands changes the weapon damage die to the listed size.
weapon_traits.versatile: Choose the listed alternate damage type when making the Strike.
weapon_traits.volley: Attacks inside the listed minimum distance take a penalty.
weapon_traits.unarmed: The attack is part of the body; it cannot normally be Disarmed and leaves hands as specified.

armor_and_shield_terms.dexterity_cap: Maximum Dexterity modifier that can contribute to AC while wearing the armor.
armor_and_shield_terms.check_penalty: Penalty to Strength- and Dexterity-based skill checks except those with the attack trait; meeting the Strength threshold removes or reduces effects as specified.
armor_and_shield_terms.speed_penalty: Reduction to Speeds while worn; meeting the Strength threshold can reduce it.
armor_and_shield_terms.strength_threshold: Strength modifier needed to avoid some armor penalties.
armor_and_shield_terms.comfort: Armor can be worn while resting without the normal poor-rest consequences.
armor_and_shield_terms.flexible: Reduces or removes check penalties for actions with the move trait as specified.
armor_and_shield_terms.noisy: Imposes its Stealth consequence unless a rule removes it.
armor_and_shield_terms.bulwark: Can substitute a fixed modifier on certain damaging Reflex saves instead of Dexterity.
armor_and_shield_terms.shield_hardness: Amount subtracted by Shield Block before remaining damage is applied.
armor_and_shield_terms.broken_threshold: At or below this HP value, an item becomes broken but is not yet destroyed.
